name: FL-17
label: Safe R

key_factors: Steube's large fundraising and cash advantage
model.rationale: The district's R+10 lean, Steube's incumbency and roughly 14-to-1 fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Republican win at about 96% all point the same way, with no polling or ratings suggesting movement. A modest shift from the baseline reflects the incumbent's financial dominance and the underfunded opposition.
model.watch: Any late independent spending or polling showing Steube underperforming the district's lean would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican incumbent Greg Steube seeks another term in a southwest Florida district that leans Republican by about ten points. He has raised over $1.3 million and holds more than $2 million on hand, while Democrat Matthew Montavon has raised under $100,000 with little cash remaining, and an independent candidate trails far behind. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Steube roughly a 96% chance of winning.

The fundamentals align with that picture: the district's partisan lean, Steube's incumbency advantage, and his financial dominance all favor the Republican side. The forecast expects Steube to win by roughly fifteen points, with the Democratic challenger needing an unexpected shift in the district or a surge of outside support to make this competitive.
